title: Damage function

definition.text: A relationship used in cost-benefit analysis that estimates the economic damage caused by an environmental change such as warming.

facts.text: Damage functions have been built for sea level rise, farm productivity and the effect of heat on labour productivity.
A common base form makes damages grow with the square of warming: 2 °C causes 4 times and 3 °C 9 times the damage of 1 °C.
Some versions add tipping points so damages speed up, or jump, once warming passes 2-3 °C.
Estimates of the social cost of carbon are highly sensitive to the damage function chosen, along with the discount rate.
A 2020 paper using an updated damage function found that around 2 °C of warming would be "optimal" in the DICE model.
Nicholas Stern argued that damage functions miss many of society's most important risks.

contested_note: Critics such as Nicholas Stern argue standard damage functions leave out major risks, and updated functions change the 'optimal' warming results.
